1.title: Multi-timeframe S/R study + five conditional templates, walk-forward tuned
1.hypothesis: Multi-timeframe S/R levels on MNQ hold price no better than distance-matched random levels once the mechanical bounce of swing levels is removed (the pilot measured every family breaking MORE often than chance), so the strongest conditional templates are breakouts through levels. Tuned per fold on prior years only, no template's stitched 2022-2025 out-of-sample excess over matched random entries is distinguishable from zero after deflation, and none approaches 600 ticks/day.
1.harness: ran on commit 837fa9f with the round-1 templates (recorded in its rounds table, templates_json); its matched null drew from all years and its deflated Sharpe used penalised trial values (both fixed for round 2, see the round-1 review).

2.title: Round-1 review applied: span-restricted null, broken-level stops, level-free control, runner exits, honest deflation
2.hypothesis: With the matched null restricted to the evaluated year, stops beyond the exact broken level (risk capped at 500 ticks), duplicate Optuna configurations collapsed, and a level-free momentum control beside the level templates: (1) the level-breakout template earns no more than the momentum control (the review measured 2R target hit 29.1% for level breaks and 29.1% for momentum-matched random bars); (2) its 2022-2025 excess over matched random is driven by 2022 and is not significant without it; (3) the runner exits (no target, breakeven, hold to the close) raise net but are not 2:1 brackets; (4) nothing approaches 600 ticks/day.
2.review_source: conditional round 1 review (reviews table, recipe round_1_20260929T043148): recommendations 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9 applied; 4 (freeze instead of tuning) and 8 (replacement templates) refuted

3.title: Pre-registered confirmation: three frozen conditional strategies on untouched NQ 2010-06..2019-06
3.hypothesis: Frozen before this run from conditional round 2 and its review (recipe round_2_20260929T054534), each parameter at its modal value across the four walk-forward folds (ties to the later fold): (1) opening_range_breakout_runner: RSI 66, stop 1.25 ATR, no target, breakeven after 1R; (2) momentum_expansion_control with the review's exit redesign: move 0.75 ATR, RSI 72, stop 2.0 ATR, 2R target, NO breakeven (on 2022-2025 this exit gave a 44% win rate and PF 1.36, chosen after seeing those years); (3) level_breakout_momentum: RSI 76, min strength 1, stop buffer 0.25 ATR, breakeven after 1.25R. PRIMARY endpoint: the equal-weight pooled daily excess over matched random entries (a level-stop strategy's null uses its real risk geometry), traded once over NQ 2010-06..2019-06 with MNQ's costs in ticks (5.56 + 1 tick stop slippage). CONFIRMED only if the pooled excess has a Newey-West t >= 2, the same with 1% trimmed off each tail has t >= 2, and at least 3 of 4 equal sub-periods are positive. Secondary: each spec's win rate and PF against the 40% / 1.33 target. The round-2 review's statistics (tuning rank correlation ~0, top-10-day share 67-76%, Reality Check p 0.15 without 2022 over 11 templates) predict NOT CONFIRMED.

4.title: Frequency and session: the frozen specs traded through ETH and RTH, both directions, with more entries per session
4.question: 600 ticks a day counts every trade in the session day, long and short, overnight (ETH) and regular hours (RTH). Rounds 1-3 capped every template at 2 entries per session inside an RTH window. Does opening the window and lifting the cap add ticks per day?
4.hypothesis: Opening the frozen specs to the overnight session, lifting the entry cap, loosening the entry thresholds (a ladder fixed here) and shortening the bar to 5m and 1m raises trades per day, but net ticks per trade falls toward minus the round-trip cost, because the cost (5.56 ticks + 1 tick stop slippage) is paid per trade while the move captured per trade shrinks with the bar and the threshold. Net ticks per session day therefore peaks at a low frequency; overnight trades net less per trade than regular-hours trades; no variant, and no sum of the three books at one setting, reaches 5% of 600 net ticks per session day on one contract. Written before any full-span round-4 result was computed (one two-month MNQ smoke run, Oct-Nov 2025, checked the code only).

spans.role: primary: never used to tune any parameter
secondary: the frozen parameters were tuned on 2019-2025 MNQ, so only the session and entry-cap changes are out of sample here

4.smoke_disclosure: Before the full run, code smoke runs on MNQ 2025-10-01..2025-12-01 (two months, 2 null seeds) were seen. They showed the three books summed at whole_day, unlimited entries, 15m, loosest reaching about +640 net ticks/day with excess t 3.3, and 1m loosest at about -800. Nothing in the variant grid was changed after the smoke except adding the 1m timeframe to the table of bar widths (it was already in the grid) and the per-year tables. The hypothesis above was written before the smoke and is kept as written.
4.price_scale_note: Ticks are a fixed 0.25 points, so the same percentage move is about ten times more ticks at MNQ 25,000 (2025) than at NQ 2,000 (2010). The 600 ticks/day question is judged per year on MNQ, and the latest full year (2025) is the price scale a live account trades at.

5.title: Time-conditioned strategies: the ETH/RTH volatility profile, time events and calendar days inside entries and exits
5.question: Overnight (ETH) and regular hours (RTH) differ in volatility and in how much they range. Does conditioning entries and exits on WHEN volatility is due to rise or fall (a causal intraday profile), on time events (Tokyo, London, 08:30 ET data, the RTH open) and on calendar days add net ticks per day, separately for ETH and RTH?
5.hypothesis: Tuned per walk-forward fold on prior years only and tested on 2022-2025: (1) seasonal_breakout_rth beats its ATR control (atr_breakout_control_rth) in stitched out-of-sample excess over matched random entries, because its stop is sized to the expected range rather than a lagging trailing ATR and it trades only into rising volatility; (2) no ETH template nets positive per trade out of sample (round 4 found 0 of 145 overnight variants positive); (3) seasonal_fade in ranging buckets does not beat zero excess after costs; (4) no template, and no sum of the templates, reaches 10% of 600 net ticks per session day. Written before any tuned result was computed; a default-parameter code smoke on MNQ 2023-06..2025-12 (overlapping the test years) was seen and nothing was changed after it.
5.profile: seasonality.build: 5-minute buckets of the 15:00-14:00 Pacific session; shape = half last-120-session mean, half last-40-same-weekday mean, of each bucket's mean |1-minute return| over its session's mean, from sessions strictly before; level = EWMA (half-life 60 minutes) of |r| / shape; expected range = sqrt(8/pi) x sqrt(pi/2) x level x sqrt(sum of shape^2 over the horizon) x price.

8.title: Round-5 review applied: the seasonal gate and exits on the confirmed momentum and level strategies, plus an order-flow gate
8.review_source: round 5 review (reviews table, recipe round_5_20260929T195018), recommendations 1, 3 and 4
8.hypothesis: Tuned per walk-forward fold on prior years only, tested 2022-2025H1 on MNQ 15m: (1) seasonal_momentum_rth and seasonal_level_breakout_rth each net more per session day than their re-tuned originals (momentum_two_to_one_control, level_breakout_momentum), mainly by trading less (paired daily net difference positive); (2) the order-flow gate (tick-rule imbalance z-score in the trade's direction) does NOT improve any seasonal template's out-of-sample excess over matched random entries, because 15-minute imbalance correlates 0.58 with the same bar's return and 0.004 with the next (measured on MNQ 2020-06..2021-06 before this pre-registration); (3) no template reaches 10% of 600 net ticks per session day. Written before any tuned result; default-parameter code smokes on MNQ 2020-06..2021-06 (outside the test years) were seen.
